targets.semanticQuestion: What exact provision procedure applies before the Final Encounter?
targets.currentState: The runtime deliberately blocks before rolling; the prior intake recorded only that a roll occurs.
searchedSources: accepted normalized requirements and source index
TTS provision dice and aid-card objects

sourceFindings.finding: The Final Encounter explicitly says to roll for Provisions before the fight.
Roll two Provision Dice per Hero; each player resolves their own wilds; all dice enter a common pool capped at 16.
The component pool contains 16 Provision Dice.

resolvedValue.rollers: each player rolls two dice for their Hero
resolvedValue.wild: the player who rolled it turns that die to any provision side
resolvedValue.timing: after the final Hamlet preparation and before the Final Encounter begins

runtimeDependencies: Persist rolled faces, post-wild faces, player choices, pool before/after and an idempotent transaction receipt; consume only in the later playable-closure branch.
targets.notes: This conclusion applies the explicitly referenced standard Roll for Provisions procedure; it does not copy the Prototype final policy.

targets.semanticQuestion: What physical deck procedure governs Darkest Dungeon encounter draws and returns?
targets.currentState: Composition was known (26 physical cards / 9 identities), but saved DeckIDs order was correctly rejected as draw policy.
searchedSources: accepted monster-deck requirement and source index
TTS deck GUID 02ef1c and all 26 contained cards

sourceFindings.finding: At Act IV, remove prior Monster cards, bring in Darkest Dungeon cards and shuffle them into the Monster deck.

Draw from the physical deck until Stance slots are filled; Front fills from Aggressive, Back from Support; duplicate names are allowed and distinguished by token color; Large monsters occupy two slots and have an explicit overflow replacement rule.
At Battle End, shuffle every Monster card used in that battle back into the Monster deck.
Gestating Heart summons a random Darkest Dungeon Monster into the next available Stance.
The physical deck contains 26 cards across nine printed identities; DeckIDs serialization order is not used.

resolvedValue.setup: shuffle the 26 Darkest Dungeon Monster cards when Act IV begins
resolvedValue.ordinaryEncounterDraw: draw the top physical card repeatedly until all four Monster Stance slots are filled

frontBackPlacement.front: first empty slot from Aggressive toward Support
frontBackPlacement.back: first empty slot from Support toward Aggressive

resolvedValue.duplicates: allowed as distinct physical cards; use printed token colors to distinguish duplicate names
resolvedValue.largeMonster: occupies two slots; if it cannot fit after three Monsters were drawn, discard the last non-large Monster drawn, shift as needed, and place the Large Monster
resolvedValue.return: at Battle End shuffle all Monster cards used in Battle back into the deck
resolvedValue.reshuffle: Battle End return-and-shuffle; no saved-order or logical-identity reshuffle
resolvedValue.gestatingSummon: select a random physical Darkest Dungeon Monster for the next available Stance; normal summon full-Stance rule prevents a summon when no Stance is available
resolvedValue.encounterComposition: the physical draw and Front/Back/Large placement procedure determines composition

targets.notes: Uniform selection among nine logical identities and serialized DeckIDs order remain forbidden. The rulebook's random Gestating summon is not evidence for equal identity weighting.

targets.semanticQuestion: Where do the Horror, its linked summons and Heroes begin?

horror.area: Room 10 Monster Aggressive marker area (source-local r10-SW)

cultistPriest.deployment: first empty Monster Stance and corresponding area when Echoing Disassembly summons it

malignantGrowth.deployment: next first empty Monster Stance and corresponding area when Echoing Disassembly summons it after Priest

targets.notes: The reserve actors have no initial area. This is a sourced absence, not a default placement.

targets.semanticQuestion: What is the complete traversable adjacency graph for Room 9, including five inset pits?
targets.currentState: Fourteen source-local areas, capacities, pit locations and marker positions are known; no accepted textual adjacency convention was found.
searchedSources: TTS GUID afa508 and tile GUID 7a3fa9
external discovery sources (not used as proof)

Movement counts Areas by Speed but does not define whether touching corners, openings, or inset pit borders create edges.
Pit Toss places a target into a rolled pit but does not define an edge out of that pit.

targets.semanticQuestion: What does each Excavation Site provision die grant and how is it added to the pool?
targets.currentState: The Room timing was known, but the runtime-specific face map was empty.

sourceFindings.finding: On entering an Excavation Site, each Hero immediately rolls one Provision die and adds it to the pool.
Provision dice faces are Food, Bandage, Potion, Torch, Tool and Wild; Wild is turned to a chosen provision side and the common pool cannot exceed 16 dice.

resolvedValue.timing: immediately on entering the Excavation Site, before its free Rest is completed

runtimeDependencies: Persist per-Hero roll and Wild choice
targets.notes: The Final and Excavation procedures are recorded separately. Their shared face map is sourced from the same physical Provision Die rules, not assumed by equality.

targets.semanticQuestion: How is no-space displacement resolved when White Cell Stalk is summoned?
targets.currentState: The prior intake quoted the generic summon rule, but exact path/tie behavior and runtime topology were not complete.

sourceFindings.finding: If the spawn area lacks space, move a Hero to the nearest available Area; if Monsters fully occupy it, players choose which Monster to move to the nearest available Area.
When more than one eligible Area exists for ordinary Monster movement, the targeted player decides, but this text does not expressly govern summon displacement.
Room 11 geometry is visible, but no normative tie-break or path-distance text is printed.

resolvedValue.heroDisplacement: a Hero must move to the nearest available Area
resolvedValue.monsterDisplacement: if Monsters fully occupy the spawn area, players choose which Monster to move to the nearest available Area
resolvedValue.playerChoice: players choose the displaced Monster only

targets.notes: The general targeted-player movement choice on p.24 is not silently extended to summon-displacement destination ties.

targets.semanticQuestion: What is the exact ordering of Ichor, lethal damage, cleanup and form transition?

external discovery sources (no accepted ruling located)

sourceFindings.finding: A Hero who attacks and Wounds the Heart suffers Blight 2 for 3 turns and the Heart heals 2; on defeat remove all other Monsters/Monster Initiative and prepare the next phase.
Target effects normally occur after other effects of a Skill, but Ichor is a defender reaction and the rule does not explicitly order a lethal case.
The ability card repeats Ichor without a lethal exception or ordering clause.

woundedReaction.trigger: a Hero attacks and Wounds the Gestating Heart

resolvedValue.defeatCleanup: remove all other Monsters and Monster Initiative Cards, then prepare the next phase

missingLeaves: whether lethal can be reversed by heal 2

targets.notes: The absence of a printed exception is not treated as permission to invent a lethal ordering.
